source_text:
INDICATION: Rectal bleeding, constipation, abnormal CT scan, rule out inflammatory bowel disease.

PREMEDICATION: See procedure nurse NCS form.

PROCEDURE: After informed consent was obtained, the patient was placed in the left lateral position and the above medications were titrated with adequate sedation. Monitoring was provided throughout the entire procedure. Digital rectal exam was performed revealing normal sphincter tone and no external hemorrhoids. The Pentax video colonoscope was inserted into rectum and advanced under direct visualization, without difficulty, to the cecum, where the cecal strap, appendiceal orifice, and the ileocecal valve were identified. The quality of the preparation was good. The colonoscope was then withdrawn while carefully examining the mucosa.

The colonic mucosa appeared normal with normal vascularity and haustral markings. No masses, polyps, AVM/s or diverticula were seen. On retroflexed view in the rectum, there are small internal hemorrhoids.

The endoscope was removed and the procedure terminated. The patient tolerated the procedure well without complications.

IMPRESSION:
1. Small internal hemorrhoids.
2. Otherwise normal colonoscopy.

PLAN: Continue fiber, increase to two tablets twice a day for a total of four tablets. Also try NuLev.

FOLLOWUP: In the office in approximately four weeks if her symptoms do not resolve.

adjudication_notes: Adjudicated from SC (Person 1) and RP (Person 2). Both captured the same procedure and findings: the colonoscopy, its indications (rectal bleeding, constipation, abnormal CT scan, rule out inflammatory bowel disease), sedation/monitoring, digital rectal exam (normal sphincter tone, no external hemorrhoids), advancement to the cecum with landmark identification, good prep quality, normal colonic mucosa, absence of masses/polyps/AVMs/diverticula, small internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion, uncomplicated tolerance, the impression, the fiber/NuLev plan, and four-week follow-up. Granularity/type decisions: SC's atomic split of the indication was kept, with 'abnormal CT scan' typed lab_value (an imaging result) rather than procedure. Endoscopic and DRE findings are typed diagnosis and the negative colon findings kept as one fact; RP had typed several of these lab_value and split the negatives into four -- a lab_value-vs-diagnosis convention for endoscopic findings the team may wish to standardize. The fiber and NuLev plan is typed medication (a supplement/medication regimen); RP typed it instruction. Impression item 1 (small internal hemorrhoids) restates the retroflexion finding and was not duplicated. Negation ('No masses, polyps, AVM/s or diverticula') and uncertainty ('rule out') preserved.
